mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted: (أنه استمع): (أن) is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ) because it is the object whose agent is not named, i.e. nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), of (أوحي). Then what comes after it with the wording (أن) is conjoined to it, so (أن) is in the position of the nominative in all of that. It is also said that (أن) was given fatḥa in the rest of the verses by referring them back to the hāʾ in (آمنا به); that is permissible although it is a genitive pronoun, on the basis of omitting the preposition, because of how often it is omitted with (أن). Conjunction with (آمنا به), in reading (أن) with fatḥa, is more complete in meaning than conjunction with (أنه استمع), because if you conjoined (وأنا ظننا), (وأنا لما سمعنا الهدى), (وأنه كان رجال من الإنس), (وأنا لمسنا) and the like to (أنه استمع), it would not be permissible, since it is not part of what was revealed to them; it is only something they reported about themselves. Kasra in all of this is clearer, and a group of the readers follow it. Fatḥa in that is by construing it according to the meaning of (آمنا به), and there is something novel [Translator's note: «بدع»; perhaps «بعد» "far-fetchedness" is intended] in the meaning, because they did not report that they believed that, when they heard the guidance, they believed in it, nor did they report that they believed that there were men...; Allah only related of them that they said that, reporting it about themselves to their companions. So kasra is more fitting for that.

mekki-muskil:6-6.t: His saying (وأنه كان رجال): the hāʾ in (أنه) is the noun of (أن), and it is the implied pronoun of the matter and the account. (رجال) is the noun of (كان) and (يعوذون) is the khabar (predicate) of (كان). (من الإنس) is a naʿt (adjective) of (رجال); that is why it is good for an indefinite noun to be the noun of (كان): when it was qualified it came close to the definite, so it may be the noun of (كان). (كان) with its noun and khabar is the khabar of (أن).

mekki-muskil:8-8.t:
His saying (فوجدناها ملئت): (وجد) takes two objects: the hāʾ is the first and (ملئت) is in the position of the second. You may also make it take one object and make (ملئت) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) with an implied (قد); the first is better. (حرسا) is accusative as a specification (tafsīr), and likewise (شهبا).
His saying (وأنه كان يقول سفيهنا على الله): the hāʾ in (أنه) is for the account, and it is the noun of (أن). In (كان) is its noun, and what comes after it is the khabar (predicate). It is also said that (سفيهنا) is the noun of (كان) and (يقول) is the khabar placed first; but this is far-fetched, because when the verb comes first it governs the noun after it. It is also permissible for (كان) to be redundant (zāʾida).

mekki-muskil:12-12.t: His saying (ولن نعجزه هربا): (هربا) is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) that stands in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial).

mekki-muskil:17-17.t: His saying (عذابا): an object of (يسلكه), meaning "into a punishment". One says (سلكه) and (أسلكه), two dialects with one meaning. It has been read (نسلكه) with ḍamma on the nūn, according to "I made it enter (أسلكته) into such-and-such".

mekki-muskil:18-18.t:
His saying (وأن المساجد لله): (أن) is in the position of the nominative by conjunction with (أنه استمع). It is also said that it is in the position of the genitive with the preposition implied; this is the school of al-Khalīl, Sībawayh and al-Kisāʾī. It is also said that it is in the position of the accusative because the preposition is absent; this is the school of a group of grammarians.
His saying (فسيعلمون من أضعف ناصرا): (من) is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) because it is interrogative, and (أضعف) is the khabar (predicate). (ناصرا) is accusative as an explanation (bayān), and likewise (عددا). The clause is in the position of the accusative governed by (سيعلمون). If you make (من) mean (الذي), it is in the position of the accusative governed by the verb, and you put (أضعف) and (أقل) in the nominative with an implied (هو), a mubtadaʾ and khabar within the ṣila (relative clause) of (من) when it means (الذي); it has no ṣila when it is interrogative.

mekki-muskil:23-23.t:
His saying (إلا بلاغا): accusative as a disjoined exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ). It is also said that it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) with an implied verb; on this view (إلا) is separated, (إن) is conditional and (لا) means (لم). The implied form is: "No one will protect me from Allah, and I will not find besides Him a refuge, if I do not convey the messages of my Lord a conveying." (الملتحد) is the refuge.
His saying (ومن يعص الله ورسوله فإن له نار جهنم): this is a condition, and its answer is the fāʾ. It is general for everyone who disobeys Allah, except what the Qur'an has made clear about forgiving minor sins by avoiding major sins, and about forgiveness for whoever repents and does righteous deeds, and what the Prophet, upon him be blessing and peace, made clear about bringing out of the Fire the monotheists among the people of sins.

mekki-muskil:25-25.t: His saying (قل إن أدري أقريب): (إن) means (ما) [negation]. (قريب) is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and (ما), meaning (الذي), is in the position of the nominative governed by (قريب) and stands in place of the khabar (predicate); or, if you wish, make it the khabar of (قريب). The clause is in the position of the accusative governed by (أدري). The hāʾ is omitted from (توعدون), referring back to (ما); the implied form is "Is the time which you are promised near?" You may also make (ما) with the verb a maṣdar, so it needs no returning pronoun.

mekki-muskil:27-27.t: His saying (إلا من ارتضى من رسول): (من) is in the position of the accusative as an exception from (أحد), because it has the meaning of a group.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t:
His saying (ليعلم أن قد): the pronoun in (ليعلم) refers back to Allah, exalted be His mention; it is also said to the Prophet, and also said to the polytheists. The pronoun in (أبلغوا) refers back to the prophets; it is also said to the angels who descend with the revelation to the prophets.
His saying (عددا): accusative as an explanation (bayān); had it been a maṣdar (verbal noun) it would have been assimilated [Translator's note: i.e. it would be «عدّا»].
